<!-- pr-reviewer: f6e53a3f40159cc089162a651957d5ed3b757efb -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thanks for this one. The door is small, it sits in one place, and the pinning tests fail on main the way the issue describes.

### What looks good
- `axis_door` runs in `verify_bodies` (`crates/sim/src/verify/engine.rs:36-42`) before the NonFinite sweep and before law (a). Every law in the engine, (a) through (f2), reads `door.path`, so the upright test from #973 (`upright::is_upright`) and the reach, rapid and posed laws all see one normalised axis. `verify` forwards to `verify_bodies`, so both public engine entries go through the door.
- Refusal is additive. A refused move keeps its stated axis, gets `Warning::NonFinite { at }` (post-blocking, with the move index), and stays judged by every law. Nothing is skipped. `one_bad_axis_refuses_only_its_own_move` pins the index.
- A unit axis passes bit for bit through `Cow::Borrowed` (the `|a|²` tolerance is 1e-12, stated in `UNIT_TOL` and in the decision note). `golden_cl` and `solid_law_goldens` are unchanged and green.
- `unit()` uses `hypot`, so tiny or subnormal axes normalise without underflow, and an overflowing length is refused rather than divided.
- `radial_rapids.rs:367` is not loosened. The `RapidInStock { at: 0 }` conviction stays, and the test now expects the added `NonFinite { at: 0 }` as well.
- The reachability search is on #1312 and the decision note links it. I spot-checked two of its claims and both hold: `cl::pose::normalize_axis` (`crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs:24`) refuses non-finite or <1e-12 axes and normalises the rest, and the project loader (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs`, `to_move`) attaches a cached axis as stored, without re-verifying it. P3 stays reasonable.
- The new module carries its provenance line, `axis_door.rs` is 87 lines, there is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests, the body has a `Changelog:` line, and the subject follows the conventional format.

### Local results (trial-merged with main `fe1cb894`, merged cleanly)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` (lib + every test binary, 59 runs) | all green: lib 104, `axis_door` 5, `radial_rapids` 15, 493 passed / 4 ignored in total |
| Pinning tests with the door neutralised locally (main behaviour) | 4 of 5 `axis_door` tests FAIL, as claimed (`the_upright_fixture_convicts_the_shank` passes on both) |
| app `verify` / `verify_arc_reading` / `tilt` / `rotary_verify` / `posed_contact` | 21 (2 ign) / 7 / 8 / 9 / 5 passed |
| app `tool_body` / `_bands` / `_drill_probe` / `_judged` / `_view` | 12 / 13 / 5 / 8 / 7 passed |
| app `golden_cl` / `solid_law_goldens` | 26 / 6 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Probes (throwaway local tests on the #938 wide-shank fixture, not pushed):
- `[0,0,1e-300]`, `[0,0,5e-324]`, `[0,0,1e-13]`, `[0,0,1e200]`: not refused, and each gets the upright verdict (ShankHit on 0 and 1).
- `|a|²` = 1+2e-12 and 1+0.5e-12 on +Z: same verdict.
- Tilts of 0.5e-9, 0.99e-9, 1.01e-9 and 2e-9 rad, each scaled by 1, 7, 1e-6 and 1e6: every scaled result equals its unit result exactly, ShankHit on 0 and 1, nothing refused.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **The other public law entries do not go through the door.** The PR body names `bands_vs_fixtures` and `rapids_vs_fixtures_spindle`. The `verify` module also exports `bands_vs_fixtures_held`, `rapids_vs_fixtures(_held)`, `bands/rapids_vs_workholding(_held)`, `mesh_refined`, `solid_hits(_walled)`, `rotary_hits`, `posed_contact`, `crossed_pairs(_all)` and `cuts_no_material`. The app calls several of them directly (`fixture_struck.rs:77-84`, `operation/generate.rs:2640,3282`, `operation/rotary_law.rs:53`, `operation/cross_part.rs:71`). Today they only see generator paths, which are normalised, and a refused axis is still blocked by `verify`'s NonFinite on the same path. A follow-up (P7) could expose the door as a small `pub` helper, or normalise on project load, so the post gate's direct calls cannot read a scaled axis from a hand-edited cached path.
2. `engine.rs:39`: `door.refused.contains(&i)` runs inside the per-move loop, so a path where every axis is bad costs O(n²). `refused` is already ascending, so `binary_search` or a `Vec<bool>` mask keeps it linear. Only degenerate input can reach this, so it is not blocking.
3. The door normalises axes the CL layer refuses: `normalize_axis` refuses any length below 1e-12, while `unit()` accepts any length above 0. That is safe (the probes give the right verdict), but the two doors disagree. Worth a line in the decision note, or the same 1e-12 floor.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
